sentences.text: Torvoneustes is unique among its relatives for having a false-ziphodont dentition, a specialized tooth arrangement.
The species T. carpenteri reached 4 to 4.7 meters in length, with some specimens suggesting an even larger size.
A related species, T. jurensis, was estimated to reach a length of 4 meters.
The species T. carpenteri was named in honor of Simon Carpenter, an amateur geologist who discovered the fossils.
The genus Torvoneustes was described by Andrade and colleagues in 2010.
The type species for the genus Torvoneustes is Dakosaurus carpenteri.
The species T. carpenteri was previously known as Dakosaurus carpenteri and Geosaurus carpenteri.
Torvoneustes belongs to the subfamily Geosaurinae.
Torvoneustes is a member of the family Metriorhynchidae.
Torvoneustes lived from the Oxfordian to the Valanginian stages, between 159 and 132.6 million years ago.
It is debated whether Torvoneustes descended from a ziphodont ancestor or if Dakosaurus and Geosaurus evolved their dentition independently.
